+# URL Shortener
+
+A small Node.js service and browser interface for creating persistent short
+links. It accepts absolute HTTP(S) destinations, returns a generated short
+URL, and redirects visitors to the original destination.
+
+## Requirements
+
+- Node.js 22 or later
+- npm
+
+## Run locally
+
+Install dependencies and start the development server:
+
+```console
+npm ci
+npm run dev
+```
+
+Open <http://localhost:3000> to use the browser interface. Links are stored in
+`data/links.json`; the directory and file are created when the first link is
+saved. Stop the server with `Ctrl+C`.
+
+For a production-style run, compile the server and browser bundle before
+starting it:
+
+```console
+npm run build
+npm start
+```
+
+## Configuration
+
+| Variable | Default | Purpose |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `PORT` | `3000` | Listening port, from 1 through 65535. |
+| `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:<PORT>` | Public origin used to construct each `shortUrl`. Set this to the externally reachable origin in deployment. |
+| `DATA_FILE` | `data/links.json` | Path to the JSON persistence file, relative to the working directory unless absolute. |
+| `CORS_ORIGIN` | `*` | Value returned in the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header. |
+
+Set variables in the shell that launches the process. For example, in
+PowerShell:
+
+```powershell
+$env:PORT = "8080"
+$env:PUBLIC_BASE_URL = "https://sho.rt"
+$env:DATA_FILE = "C:\url-shortener\data\links.json"
+$env:CORS_ORIGIN = "https://app.example.com"
+npm start
+```
+
+The service fails at startup when `PORT` is invalid or when an existing data
+file does not match the expected format.
+
+## Use the API
+
+All JSON responses use `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.
+
+### Create a short link
+
+```console
+curl --request POST http://localhost:3000/api/links \
+  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  --data "{\"url\":\"https://example.com/articles/getting-started\"}"
+```
+
+A newly created link returns `201 Created`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "code": "V1StGXR8",
+  "url": "https://example.com/articles/getting-started",
+  "shortUrl": "http://localhost:3000/V1StGXR8",
+  "createdAt": "2026-08-28T08:30:00.000Z"
+}
+```
+
+Codes and timestamps are generated by the service. Submitting the same
+normalized destination again returns the existing record with `200 OK`.
+
+The `url` value must:
+
+- be a non-empty absolute URL no longer than 2,048 characters;
+- use the `http` or `https` scheme; and
+- not contain a username or password.
+
+### Inspect a link
+
+Replace the example code with the `code` returned during creation:
+
+```console
+curl http://localhost:3000/api/links/V1StGXR8
+```
+
+A successful lookup returns `200 OK` and the same JSON representation as the
+create operation.
+
+### Follow a short link
+
+Opening `http://localhost:3000/V1StGXR8` in a browser responds with
+`302 Found` and redirects to the stored destination. To inspect the redirect
+without following it:
+
+```console
+curl --include --max-redirs 0 http://localhost:3000/V1StGXR8
+```
+
+The response includes the destination in its `Location` header and
+`Cache-Control: no-store`.
+
+### Check service health
+
+```console
+curl http://localhost:3000/health
+```
+
+```json
+{"status":"ok"}
+```
+
+## Errors
+
+Errors have a stable envelope:
+
+```json
+{
+  "error": {
+    "code": "INVALID_URL",
+    "message": "url must use http or https"
+  }
+}
+```
+
+For example, an unsupported URL scheme returns `400 Bad Request`:
+
+```console
+curl --request POST http://localhost:3000/api/links \
+  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  --data "{\"url\":\"ftp://example.com/file\"}"
+```
+
+| Status | Code | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `400` | `INVALID_JSON` | The request body is not valid JSON. |
+| `400` | `INVALID_URL` | The destination is missing or violates the URL requirements. |
+| `400` | `INVALID_CODE` | The code is not 6-32 URL-safe letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. |
+| `404` | `LINK_NOT_FOUND` | No stored link or route matches the request. |
+| `405` | `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` | The route does not support the HTTP method. |
+| `413` | `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | The request body exceeds 4,096 bytes. |
+| `500` | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | An unexpected server error occurred. |
+
+## Development checks
+
+```console
+npm run typecheck
+npm run lint
+npm test
+```
+
+`npm test` runs the unit and integration suites and enforces at least 80%
+coverage for lines, functions, and branches.

+# URL Shortener UX Specification
+
+## Scope and experience principles
+
+This specification covers one task: enter a long URL, create a shortened URL,
+view the result, and copy it. It is framework-neutral because the repository has
+no existing application, components, or design tokens.
+
+Keep the experience on one page with one primary action. Do not add accounts,
+saved history, analytics, link editing, expiration controls, QR codes, or custom
+aliases without a separate requirement.
+
+## Information architecture
+
+Use a single `<main>` landmark containing:
+
+1. A page heading and one-sentence instruction.
+2. The shortening form.
+3. A result or status region in the same location below the form.
+
+Recommended content:
+
+- Page heading: **Shorten a URL**
+- Instruction: **Enter a long URL to create a shorter link.**
+- Field label: **Long URL**
+- Placeholder: `https://example.com/very/long/link`
+- Primary action: **Shorten URL**
+- Result heading: **Your shortened URL**
+- Copy action: **Copy**
+- Retry action for service failures: **Try again**
+
+The label and instructions must remain visible; the placeholder is only an
+example and must not act as the label.
+
+## Primary flow
+
+1. On load, keyboard focus remains at the browser's normal starting position.
+   The page presents the heading, instruction, URL field, and submit button.
+2. The user enters a URL and submits with the button or Enter while focus is in
+   the field.
+3. Client-side validation runs. Invalid input keeps focus on the field and
+   exposes a specific inline error. Valid input proceeds to loading.
+4. During loading, the entered URL remains visible, editing is disabled, and the
+   submit button reads **Shortening...**. Only one request may be active.
+5. On success, the result region displays the complete shortened URL as a
+   working link followed by **Copy**. Focus moves to the result heading.
+6. Activating **Copy** copies the exact shortened URL. The button temporarily
+   reads **Copied** and a polite live-region message confirms **Shortened URL
+   copied.** Focus remains on the button.
+7. The user may replace the long URL and submit again. Starting a new request
+   clears the previous result when submission begins, not while the user edits.
+
+## State specification
+
+| State | Presentation and behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| Default / empty | Empty field; enabled submit button. Empty input submitted as whitespace shows **Enter a URL.** Do not show an error before submission. |
+| Editing | Preserve user input exactly while typing. A prior field error clears only after the value changes and is revalidated, or on the next submit. A previous successful result remains available until a new valid submission begins. |
+| Loading | Preserve the submitted value; disable field and submit action; change button text to **Shortening...** and expose `aria-busy="true"` on the status region. Do not use an indeterminate spinner without visible text. Ignore duplicate activation while pending. |
+| Success | Show **Your shortened URL**, the full shortened URL as an external link, and **Copy**. Do not truncate the accessible link name or copy value. Visual middle truncation is allowed on narrow screens if the full value remains available to assistive technology and through copy. |
+| Validation error | Show one inline message associated with the field. Use **Enter a URL.** for empty input and **Enter a valid URL beginning with http:// or https://.** for unsupported or malformed input. Preserve input and place focus on the field. |
+| Service error | Keep the submitted URL available. Show **We couldn't shorten this URL. Try again.** and a **Try again** button. Retry submits the same value once; the user may instead edit it. Never present an error response as a successful result. |
+| Copy error | Keep the link visible and selectable. Announce **Couldn't copy the URL. Select and copy it manually.** Do not change the button to **Copied**. |
+
+### Edge-case behavior
+
+- Trim leading and trailing whitespace for validation and submission without
+  altering whitespace inside the URL.
+- Accept only absolute `http://` and `https://` URLs. The backend remains the
+  authority for maximum length and security restrictions; display its safe,
+  user-actionable validation message beside the field when available.
+- Preserve query strings, fragments, letter case, and percent encoding in the
+  submitted value.
+- If the same URL is submitted again, treat the returned short URL normally;
+  do not promise deduplication.
+- If an earlier request completes after a later request, render only the latest
+  request's outcome.
+- A network failure, timeout, rate limit, or unavailable service uses the
+  service-error state. Do not expose stack traces, status codes, or raw server
+  responses.
+- A shortened URL longer than its container wraps or visually truncates without
+  causing horizontal page scrolling. Copy always uses the full value.
+- After a successful copy, restore the button label to **Copy** after a short
+  interval or when focus leaves it. Repeated copy activation restarts feedback.
+
+## Responsive layout
+
+- Use the project's established tokens and components when they exist. Until
+  then, implementation should define semantic tokens rather than hard-coded
+  one-off values.
+- Center a single content column with a readable maximum width of approximately
+  40rem and at least 1rem inline page padding.
+- Below 30rem, stack the input and submit button with both at full width. Stack
+  the result link and copy button if they cannot fit without clipping.
+- At 30rem and above, the input and submit button may share a row; the field
+  takes remaining width and the action retains its intrinsic width.
+- Allow text wrapping and content-driven height. The interface must remain
+  usable at 320 CSS pixels wide and at 400% zoom without two-dimensional page
+  scrolling.
+- Touch targets must be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, with 44 by 44 preferred
+  for primary and copy actions.
+
